PullRequest.Title: ci: only run the chat-lib pipeline for changes in extensions/copilot
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

The chat-lib npm package pipeline (`extensions/copilot/build/npm-package.yml`) ran on every push to `main` and `release/*`, even when the push didn't touch Copilot. This adds a path filter so its CI trigger only fires when a push changes files under `extensions/copilot`.

Reviewer notes:
- Manual runs, including the publish options, are unchanged.
- The pipeline definition is under `extensions/copilot`, so changes to it still trigger a run.
- `npm-package-next.yml`, which publishes the `next` tag and is triggered by the main VS Code pipeline, is unchanged.
- The chat-lib build also reads a few files outside `extensions/copilot`: `build/azure-pipelines/common/install-pnpm.yml`, `src/vscode-dts/*.d.ts` and `src/typings/thenable.d.ts`. Changes limited to those files will no longer trigger this pipeline on their own.

How to test:
- Checked that the `trigger` block parses to the expected branch and path filters with a YAML parser: passed.
- The trigger itself can only be confirmed in Azure Pipelines after merge. A push that changes only files outside `extensions/copilot` should not start a run; a push that changes files under `extensions/copilot` should.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A repository-wide branch trigger eagerly scheduled dependency installation, extraction, compilation, and a three-platform test matrix for unrelated pushes; batching could merge queued pushes but could not avoid this work when an unrelated push produced a run.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Unrelated main/release pushes consumed Azure agents and incurred unnecessary package-network, filesystem, build, and test work, increasing CI resource use and potential queue latency.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The new path include prevents unrelated repository pushes from scheduling the chat-lib build/test pipeline while preserving runs for Copilot changes and manual invocation.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before this PR, the top-level trigger included every push to main and release/* with no path restriction. Each such trigger reaches build-chat-lib.yml, which installs pnpm, runs two frozen dependency installs, extracts chat-lib, and builds it; the pipeline also executes chat-lib tests on Linux, macOS, and Windows. The added paths.include at RIGHT lines 7-9 limits that unchanged expensive path to pushes touching extensions/copilot.

Scenarios.Scenario: Push to main or release/* that changes only files outside extensions/copilot
Scenarios.CriticalPath: This is off the product runtime critical path but on the repository CI critical path: before the diff, the chat-lib pipeline and its agent allocation had to complete to finish that pipeline run; after the diff, no chat-lib run is created for this scenario.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run frozen pnpm dependency installation for the extension extraction root and then for chat-lib in the build path and each platform test path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, each unrelated batched push run reached two pnpm installs in the build path plus two in each of three platform test paths (up to eight install invocations); cache warmth can reduce fetched bytes but not eliminate invocation and filesystem work. After the diff, zero for this pipeline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The unfiltered branch trigger scheduled this boundary for unrelated pushes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These installs occupied CI agents and preceded chat-lib build/tests; the diff removes them entirely from unrelated pushes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extract and compile chat-lib, then run its tests on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, one extraction/build in the build path and one per platform test path, plus three test executions, for each resulting batched unrelated-push run; after the diff, none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every main/release push reaching the trigger performed the unchanged build and platform-test work regardless of changed path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This work consumed agents and determined completion time for the unnecessary chat-lib pipeline run; it is eliminated for this scenario.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The cost previously scaled with the number of main/release push batches that contained no Copilot changes; Azure batching reduced queued-run count but did not make an executed run path-aware.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: trigger.batch limits queued branch runs by batching while a run is active. Within a run, the shared npm-package template defines one build path and tests for Linux, macOS, and Windows; agent-pool scheduling determines actual parallelism. The diff reduces this scenario from one batched pipeline run to zero rather than increasing concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Before the change, Azure's batch trigger could coalesce queued pushes, but every resulting run still performed frozen pnpm installs and builds; warm package caches could reduce downloads but not process startup, lockfile resolution, extraction, compilation, or tests. After the path filter, this pipeline has no cache interaction because it is not scheduled.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the prior branch-only trigger, added path include, and transitive install/build/test steps are directly evidenced. This is a performance improvement, recorded as a regression fix, not a finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact agent duration, package-cache hit rate, push frequency, and shared-template job concurrency are not visible, but the eliminated subprocess/install cardinality is explicit in the checked-in pipeline and templates.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The diff removes eager CI work for unrelated pushes and adds no replacement boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Push to main or release/* that changes extensions/copilot
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing chat-lib dependency installation, extraction, build, and three-platform tests remain on this pipeline's CI critical path; the added filter is evaluated before scheduling and adds no work inside the run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install extension and chat-lib dependencies with pnpm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged: two install invocations in the build path and two per platform test path, subject to shared-template execution and package caches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same matching branch push scheduled the same dependency-install work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Still precedes build/tests exactly as before; the new path predicate does not move or duplicate it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extract, build, and test chat-lib across the configured build and platform paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged for a matching trigger: build path plus Linux, macOS, and Windows tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical pipeline body ran for Copilot changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains the pipeline's normal work and is neither added nor delayed by the filter.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Copilot-changing push batches; effective trigger cardinality remains one run per Azure batch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Azure batch behavior and the shared template's build/platform-test scheduling are unchanged; one matching batched trigger still feeds the same matrix.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold and warm package behavior is unchanged: frozen pnpm installs may use package-manager caches, while extraction, compilation, and tests still run. The path filter matches this scenario, so cache keys and negative-cache behavior are unaffected.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed include matches extensions/copilot and leaves the pipeline body untouched.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Shared external template details and agent timing are unavailable, but they are unchanged by this one-hunk trigger edit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression because matching pushes execute the same work at the same effective cardinality and concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Push that changes only an external file consumed by chat-lib extraction or setup, such as src/vscode-dts, src/typings/thenable.d.ts, or build/azure-pipelines/common/install-pnpm.yml
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed trigger removes the chat-lib npm-package validation run from this push's CI path. Any loss of validation is correctness/coverage, not a performance regression; no new work is placed on an important path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and copy referenced VS Code declaration files, including src/typings/thenable.d.ts, into extracted chat-lib output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, once per extraction in the build and platform test paths of the resulting run; after the diff, zero in this pipeline for an external-only change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The broad branch trigger caused extraction to consume these external inputs even when they were the only changed files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The filesystem work is removed with the pipeline run rather than moved elsewhere by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute the repository installPnpm.ts setup step through the included pipeline template.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, once in each build/test path that includes the setup template; after the diff, zero for an external-only push in this pipeline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The unfiltered trigger scheduled the setup step for these pushes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Removed from this pipeline's CI path; no replacement subprocess is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: External-only main/release push batches, after Azure trigger batching.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: This pipeline's effective concurrency becomes zero for these external-only pushes. Other pipelines retain their own unchanged scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The filtered npm-package pipeline does not run, so it performs no cold or warm cache operations. The separate npm-package-next pipeline remains triggered by the VS Code release pipeline, but that independent behavior is unchanged by this diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the filter suppresses this pipeline and its boundaries; implications for validation are outside the performance-only focus.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether these external inputs change frequently is unknown. That affects saved CI work, not the absence of a regression mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. The change reduces CI work; the changed validation coverage is not independently a performance regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed hunk and traced matching, unrelated, and externally consumed-file push scenarios through dependency installation, extraction, filesystem copies, compilation, and the platform test matrix. No diff-introduced performance issue was found. The prior repository-wide eager pipeline execution was identified and recorded as a concrete regression fix with its introducing commit.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
